findings.title: MixedGraph no longer cloned; may alias plan graph
findings.message: The code used to store `plan.graph.Clone()`; it now stores `physical` directly. A graph with no blocks may come back from `PhysicalGraph()` sharing its Components slice and maps with `plan.graph`. In that case, any change the mixed network makes to `MixedGraph` would leak into the sweep plan. `solveDCOperatingPoint` in the same diff still clones.
findings.suggestion: Keep the defensive copy, `compiled.MixedGraph = physical.Clone()`, unless `PhysicalGraph` is guaranteed to return a deep copy.

findings.title: Test indexes DC result with net map from a different compile
findings.message: `solveDCOperatingPoint` now compiles the physical (flattened) graph, so `dc.Nodes` uses the physical compile's net numbering. The test looks up the node index in a compile of the block-level graph instead. The two numberings are not guaranteed to match. The assertion may therefore check the wrong node, passing or failing by coincidence.
findings.suggestion: Take the net index from the same compiled graph the solver used, i.e. compile `g.PhysicalGraph()`. Alternatively, check the value through the returned TraceSample.

findings.title: AC assertions pass vacuously on empty result
findings.message: If the sweep returns zero points, the AC loop runs zero times and the transfer-function check silently passes. `point.AC[0]` would also panic if AC is empty.
findings.suggestion: Assert that `len(r.Points) > 0` and that `len(point.AC) > 0` before comparing.
